newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia would like new Russia oil export pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Latvia would like new Russia oil export pipeline.

text.p: Latvia has suggested to Russian officials that a new pipeline for Russian oil be built between their two countries, Latvian Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans said on Monday.
Latvia's Ventspils port is one of the main outlets for Russian crude, which is served by two pipelines.
Latvia wants to maintain its position as an export outlet in the face of increased competition from other Baltic ports and as Russia plans to build its own terminals.
"We would be glad to start discussing the construction of a new oil pipeline," Krishtopans told a news conference.
He was speaking after a three-day visit to Russia, where he met oil transit officials, but he did not give any details of where the new pipeline should be built or how much it would cost.
Krishtopans also suggested that Russia introduce higher tariffs for its oil product exports, which at $2.75 per tonne were causing a loss for the joint Latvian-Russian transit company Latrostrans.
He said he would back a rise in the tariff of around 60 U.S. cents but at the same time granting discounts to the largest customers.
